Task 4
first we are placing the subjects in three different groups based on blood pressure, optimal is less than 121, borderline is from 121 to 130 inclusive, and high is above 130. This is done for both the treatment and the placebo groups.

bp_list$treatment$status= character(20)
bp_list$placebo$status= character(10)
#nrow just gets the number of rows, easier than remembering how many rows it has

for (i in 1:nrow(bp_list$treatment)) {
  if (bp_list$treatment$post_bp[i] <= 120) {
    bp_list$treatment$status[i] <- "optimal"
  } else if (bp_list$treatment$post_bp[i] <= 130) {
    bp_list$treatment$status[i] <- "borderline"
  } else {
    bp_list$treatment$status[i] <- "high"
  }
}

If the working directory is myfolder/homework/, the relative path needed to access myfolder/MyData.csv is ../MyData.csv. The .. moves up one directory from the homework folder to the myfolder folder.
Some major benefits of using R Projects are that they keep all files for a project organized in one location, which make relative file paths easier to use and provide a consistent working directory. This also makes it easier to use Git and GitHub for a project.
Git is a version control system that tracks changes made to files and allows users to keep different versions of their work. GitHub is an online platform that hosts Git repositories and makes it easy to store, share, and collaborate on projects.
Two main differences between a tibble and a data.frame are:

Tibbles print only the rows and columns that fit on the screen instead of the entire data set
Tibbles are more strict about how they handle variables and do not automatically change things such as variable names or data types in the way traditional data frames might
